q: x has the type string | number. Why does x.length not compile?
options: A number has no length, and the compiler only allows what every member of the union has
Strings do not have a length property in TypeScript
x must be declared with let for length to work
length can only be used inside a function
why: On a union you can only use what every member has. A number has no length, so the compiler asks you to narrow first, for example with typeof x === "string".

q: Which checks make a union type smaller in the compiler?
why: typeof, in and instanceof are real checks that the compiler follows. x as string is not a check. It only tells the compiler to believe you, and it disappears at run time.

q: count has the type number | undefined. The check if (count) is a safe way to test that count has a value.
why: No. 0 is falsy, so a real count of 0 goes to the else branch. Use count !== undefined. The compiler even keeps number | undefined in the else branch, but it does not stop you.

q: Put the steps in order: how a switch on a kind field catches a new shape that nobody handled.
items: Every member has a kind field with one exact word
A switch on s.kind narrows s to one member in each case
In the default branch s is never, and assertNever(s) compiles
A new member is added to the union and no case is written for it
In the default branch s is now the new member, so tsc reports an error in the switch
why: The kind field lets the switch narrow. With all cases handled, the default is never. A new member breaks that, so the compiler points at the function that forgot it.

q: A function has default: return 0 instead of assertNever(s). A new shape is added to the union. What happens?
options: No error from the compiler, and the new shape quietly gets 0
The program crashes when it starts
tsc changes the default to never by itself
why: I ran this: areaQuiet with a triangle printed 0 and tsc was quiet. Only assertNever, a function that accepts never, makes the compiler fail when a case is missing.

q: Inside the default branch of a switch where every kind has a case, the compiler believes the value has the type ______. (one word)
why: Nothing is left after every member is handled, so the type is never, the type with no values. That is why assertNever(x: never) compiles there.
